```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

#Packates needed
```{r}
library(dplyr)
```

#Upload data to the global environment. 
#We are using the summer and winter surveys from the Medicare Beneficiaries survey
```{r}
winter<- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Asteck-WashU-MPH/ADA_Final_Project/refs/heads/main/sfpuf2023_2_winter.csv")
summer<- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Asteck-WashU-MPH/ADA_Final_Project/refs/heads/main/sfpuf2023_3_summer.csv")
fall<- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Asteck-WashU-MPH/ADA_Final_Project/refs/heads/main/sfpuf2023_1_fall.csv")
```

#Check the datasets
```{r}
anyDuplicated(winter$PUF_ID)    
anyDuplicated(summer$PUF_ID)  
anyDuplicated(fall$PUF_ID)

common_ids <- Reduce(intersect, list(summer$PUF_ID, winter$PUF_ID, fall$PUF_ID))
length(common_ids)
```
#Merge the winter and summer datasets
```{r}
Merged <-merge(winter, summer, by = "PUF_ID")

merged<- merge(Merged, fall, by= "PUF_ID")

```

#Select the needed variables so that it is more usable
```{r}
select<- merged %>% select(PUF_ID, DEM_CBSA, #metro area
                           PVS_FLUSHOT, #flushot
                           DEM_IPR_IND, #poverty ratio category
                           DEM_SEX, #male or female
                           DEM_RACE, #race category
                           DEM_AGE, #age group
                           DEM_EDU, #education category
                           HLT_DTBLGTPL, #Has trouble getting places
                           HLT_FUNC_LIM #IADLs and ADLs
                           )
```

#Check the available data for missingness
```{r}
sum(!complete.cases(select))          # number of responses with at least one NA
mean(!complete.cases(select)) * 100   # as a percentage
sum(complete.cases(select))           # number of fully complete responses
```
#Hooray- still have a really good number of cases

#Rename the variables so that it is less confusing
```{r}
select_rename<- select %>%
  rename(flu_shot= PVS_FLUSHOT,metro_cat= DEM_CBSA, poverty_cat= DEM_IPR_IND,sex= DEM_SEX, race_cat= DEM_RACE,age= DEM_AGE, edu_cat= DEM_EDU, transport_cat= HLT_DTBLGTPL, disabled_cat= HLT_FUNC_LIM)
```

#Check flu vaccine data
```{r}
table(select_rename$flu_shot, useNA = "ifany")
class(select_rename$flu_shot)
```
It is a character variable and we want 0s and 1s so we are recoding based on the code book. 

#Convert vaccine variable to be 1 for vaccine, 0 for non-vaccine, and NA for "don't know" 
```{r}
clean_variables <- select_rename %>%
  mutate(flu_shot = case_when(
    flu_shot == "1" ~ 1,
    flu_shot == "2" ~ 0,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$flu_shot)                  
table(clean_variables$flu_shot, useNA = "ifany")
```
The class says numeric which is what we want and the categories match up pretty closely with the code book so that makes sense as well. 

#Check metro residence variable
```{r}
table(clean_variables$metro_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$metro_cat)
```
The "exposure" we are looking at is living in a rural place so we will code non-metro as 1 and metro as 0. 

#Recode metro residence: 
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(metro_cat = case_when(
    metro_cat == "1" ~ 0,
    metro_cat == "2" ~ 1,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$metro_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$metro_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
Looks good

#Check poverty variable
```{r}
table(clean_variables$poverty_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$poverty_cat)
```
#Clean poverty variable so that it is numeric and the highest income group is the reference
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(poverty_cat = case_when(
    poverty_cat == "1" ~ 4,
    poverty_cat == "2" ~ 3,
    poverty_cat == "3" ~ 2,
    poverty_cat == "4" ~ 1,
    poverty_cat == "5" ~ 0,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$poverty_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$poverty_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
#categories: 
#4: <=100% of the Federal Poverty Level                                     
#3: >100% and <=120% of the Federal Poverty                                 
#2: >120% and <=135% of the Federal Poverty                                 
#1: >135% and <=200% of the Federal Poverty                                 
#0: >200% of the Federal Poverty Level 

#check race variable
```{r}
table(clean_variables$race_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$race_cat)
```
#clean race variable to be numeric with non-hispanic white as the reference group
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(race_cat = case_when(
    race_cat == "1" ~ 0,
    race_cat == "2" ~ 1,
    race_cat == "3" ~ 2,
    race_cat == "4" ~ 3,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$race_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$race_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
0:Non-Hispanic white                                                       
1:Non-Hispanic black                                                       
2:Hispanic                                                                 
3:Other

#Check sex variable: 
```{r}
table(clean_variables$sex, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$sex)
```
#Make male 0 and female 1 and convert to numeric variable
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(sex = case_when(
    sex == "1" ~ 0,
    sex == "2" ~ 1,

    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$sex)                  
table(clean_variables$sex, useNA = "ifany")
```
#Check age variable:
```{r}
table(clean_variables$age, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$age)
```
#correct age variable: Exclude those under 65
```{r}
clean_variables <- clean_variables %>%
  filter(age != 1)
```

#change age category based on the two groups: 
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(age = case_when(
    age == "2" ~ 0,
    age == "3" ~ 1,

    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$age)                  
table(clean_variables$age, useNA = "ifany")
```
0:Age 65-74 years                                                          
1:Age 75+ years 

#check education variable: 
```{r}
table(clean_variables$edu_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$edu_cat)
```
#Create NA out of don't know or refused. : 
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(edu_cat = case_when(
    edu_cat == "1" ~ 0,
    edu_cat == "2" ~ 1,
    edu_cat == "3" ~ 2,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$edu_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$edu_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
0:Less than high school                                                    
1:High school or vocational/technical/business                             
2:More than high school

#Check transportation variable: 
```{r}
table(clean_variables$transport_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$transport_cat)
```
#Make don't know into NA, Make the exposure of "Yes" to has trouble getting places 1, and "no"=0
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(transport_cat = case_when(
    transport_cat == "1" ~ 1,
    transport_cat == "2" ~ 0,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$transport_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$transport_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
#Check disability categories: 
```{r}
table(clean_variables$disabled_cat, useNA = "ifany")
class(clean_variables$disabled_cat)
```
#Create binary variable: 1=disability, 2=no disability. 
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(disabled_bin = case_when(
    disabled_cat == "0" ~ 0,
    disabled_cat == "1" ~ 1,
    disabled_cat == "2" ~ 1,
    disabled_cat == "3" ~ 1,
    disabled_cat == "4" ~ 1,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$disabled_bin)                  
table(clean_variables$disabled_bin, useNA = "ifany")
```
#Make second variable that accounts for variation in disability. 
```{r}
clean_variables<- clean_variables %>% 
  mutate(disabled_cat = case_when(
    disabled_cat == "0" ~ 0,
    disabled_cat == "1" ~ 1,
    disabled_cat == "2" ~ 2,
    disabled_cat == "3" ~ 3,
    disabled_cat == "4" ~ 4,
    TRUE           ~ NA_real_    
  ))

#sanity check 
class(clean_variables$disabled_cat)                  
table(clean_variables$disabled_cat, useNA = "ifany")
```
#Rename final dataset for analysis: 
```{r}
clean_medicare<- clean_variables
```
